hero.headline: Jupiter, Delray Beach, Palm Beach County firefighters deploy to Venezuela for earthquake search and rescue
hero.teaser: First responders from Jupiter, Delray Beach and Palm Beach County fire departments deployed to Venezuela as part of a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force with less than 24 hours notice.
hero.body:
First responders from Jupiter, Delray Beach, and Palm Beach County fire departments have joined a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force heading to Venezuela to help with relief efforts following an earthquake. Jupiter Fire Rescue contributed two firefighters to the deployment, which totals approximately 80 personnel from the region. The team received their deployment orders with less than 24 hours notice and is expected to remain in Venezuela for at least two weeks.

The primary focus of the mission involves conducting search and rescue operations in collapsed structures of all sizes, from large commercial buildings to residential homes. To accomplish this work effectively, the rescue team packed specialized heavy-duty equipment designed for breaking through debris, cutting through materials, breaching barriers, and stabilizing unsafe structures. They also brought technical rope rescue tools to assist in extracting people from difficult-to-reach locations within damaged buildings.

Stephen Shaw, deputy fire chief of operations for Jupiter Fire Rescue, emphasized that the deployment demonstrates the department's core mission and values. "This right here represents one of these situations where, they need help people need help and for us at Jupiter Fire Rescue, if someone needs help we go," Shaw said. He noted that responding to humanitarian crises abroad reflects how the department approaches its responsibility to assist people in urgent need, regardless of location.

Shaw also pointed out that the deployment will have positive effects for Jupiter Fire Rescue long after the team returns home. The experience gained and skills practiced during search and rescue operations in Venezuela will strengthen the department's capabilities as it continues to develop and expand. "And when they come back the learning that has taken place and the skills that they have been practicing is only going to benefit us internally as we continue to grow our fire department," Shaw said. By sending personnel on international disaster response missions, the department gains practical experience and expertise that enhances training and readiness for future emergencies in their own community.

cards.headline: Florida sees 200% spike in fatal road rage crashes, second-highest increase in nation
cards.body:
A new study by Grigor Law Injury Car Accident Lawyers reveals a disturbing trend in Florida's traffic fatalities. The analysis of data from the Fatality Analysis Reporting System operated by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration shows that fatal crashes involving road rage nearly tripled in the state between 2023 and 2024. The number of deadly anger-related driving incidents jumped from 12 to 36 in just one year, representing a 200% increase that places Florida second in the nation for this troubling statistic.

Only Wyoming experienced a higher percentage increase in fatal road rage crashes during the same period, with a 300% spike. However, Wyoming's raw numbers tell a different story. The state saw fatal incidents rise from just one to four, far below Florida's alarming total of 36 deaths. Texas ranked third nationally with an 83.33% increase in road rage fatalities, climbing from six incidents in 2023 to 11 in 2024. These three states clearly stand out as having the most significant year-over-year increases in deadly anger-related driving confrontations.

Several other states in the top 10 for road rage fatalities experienced lower percentage increases but recorded substantially higher raw numbers than Florida. Alabama ranked seventh with a 27.03% jump, but the figures climbed from 74 fatalities to 94, dwarfing Florida's numbers. Colorado came in eighth with just an 8.33% increase, yet the state reported far more total incidents than any other state, rising from 120 in 2023 to 130 in 2024. South Carolina also had significant raw numbers despite minimal percentage growth, seeing only a 1.82% increase but recording 55 crashes jumping to 56.

The study examined data from 2020 through 2024 and highlights the growing pattern of aggressive driving incidents turning deadly on roadways across the country. While Florida's percentage increase places it second nationally, the raw numbers reveal a serious public safety concern. The data suggests that anger management issues among Florida drivers are creating a dangerous environment on the state's highways and roads. The findings underscore the need for awareness about the consequences of aggressive driving behavior and the deadly toll it takes on communities.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis signs third revision of Live Local Act to expand affordable housing
cards.teaser: Ron DeSantis signed the updated Live Local Act this month after it was approved by the House and Senate, marking the third revision since the measure was originally approved three years ago.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the updated Live Local Act this month after it was approved by the House and Senate. The Senate bill (SB 962) was sponsored by Fleming Island Republican Sen. Jennifer Bradley, and the House companion (HB 837) was sponsored by Coral Gables Republican Rep. This marks the third time the Live Local Act has been revised since it was originally approved in 2023.

The law requires cities and counties to allow apartment buildings or mixed-use housing projects in many areas currently zoned for commercial or industrial use, if at least 40% of the units are set aside as affordable housing for 30 years. That can also apply to land owned by local governments, school districts or large religious institutions. The law limits how much local governments can restrict the height or design of these developments, making it harder for cities and counties to block them through zoning rules. The latest revision would exclude farms and farm operations from the land-use categories eligible for its development preemptions. The measure will allow more dwelling unit types, limit local restrictions and protect financial sources for buying homes. The original intent of the measure was to spur construction of affordable and workforce housing across Florida through funding, tax incentives and zoning preemptions. The original iteration fell under criticism from watchdog groups such as Florida TaxWatch for falling short on "missing middle" renters, households that earn too much to qualify for affordable housing subsidies but not enough to comfortably pay market rents in their area.

cards.headline: Off-duty Martin County Fire Rescue lieutenant recovers body of missing diver near Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: An off-duty Martin County Fire Rescue lieutenant recovered the body of a missing diver near Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
An off-duty Martin County Fire Rescue lieutenant recovered the body of a missing diver near Fort Pierce. The diver was found dead in the water.

The recovery operation involved the Martin County Fire Rescue lieutenant who was off duty at the time of the incident. The diver had been reported missing before being found deceased.

Martin County Fire Rescue personnel were involved in the recovery effort. The incident occurred in waters near Fort Pierce.

The recovery took place on Sunday. Details about the diver's identity and the circumstances that led to the death were not released.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman dies after SUV rolls backward in driveway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman died after being struck by an SUV in a driveway.
cards.body:
A woman in Port St. Lucie died after an SUV rolled backward and struck her in a driveway. The incident occurred Sunday in Port St. Lucie.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the fatal accident. The woman was knocked down by the SUV as it rolled backward.

cards.headline: Jupiter firefighters deploy to Venezuela for earthquake search and rescue mission
cards.body:
Two firefighters from Jupiter Fire Rescue have been sent to Venezuela as part of a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force responding to earthquake relief efforts. The deployment happened with minimal notice, giving the firefighters less than 24 hours to prepare before heading to the region. They are expected to stay in Venezuela for at least two weeks as part of the ongoing relief operation.

The Jupiter firefighters are part of a larger contingent of 80 first responders drawn from fire departments across South Florida, including agencies from Delray Beach and Palm Beach County. These rescue workers have been equipped with specialized tools and machinery needed for their mission, including heavy-duty equipment designed for breaking, cutting, breaching, and stabilizing structures. The team also brought technical rope rescue tools to help them navigate dangerous environments and safely extract people from collapsed buildings. The focus of their work will be conducting search and rescue operations in structures that have been damaged or destroyed, ranging from large commercial buildings to residential homes.

Stephen Shaw, deputy fire chief of operations for Jupiter Fire Rescue, explained that the deployment represents the department's core mission of responding to people in need wherever that need exists. "This right here represents one of these situations where they need help, people need help and for us at Jupiter Fire Rescue, if someone needs help we go," Shaw said. The decision to send firefighters reflects the department's values and commitment to lending assistance during crises, even when it requires rapid deployment on short notice to international locations.

Beyond the immediate humanitarian impact, Shaw noted that the mission will provide valuable benefits to Jupiter Fire Rescue when the firefighters return home. The experience gained from working in challenging conditions and applying rescue skills in real-world scenarios will enhance the department's overall capabilities. "When they come back the learning that has taken place and the skills that they have been practicing is only going to benefit us internally as we continue to grow our fire department," Shaw said. This approach to emergency response demonstrates how deployment to assist other regions can strengthen local fire departments through the practical experience and training their personnel gain in the field.

cards.headline: Vero Beach organization collects earthquake relief supplies for Venezuela through Saturday
cards.body:
A Vero Beach-based organization is collecting donations for Venezuelan communities affected by a devastating 7.5 magnitude earthquake. Latinas Nexus Network is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to gather essential supplies for those impacted by the disaster. The effort is being coordinated by founders Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino, along with Heidi Ramirez. Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Hwy, Vero Beach, FL 32962, through Saturday, June 27, 2026, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.

Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and currently lives in Vero Beach, explained that while her family in Caracas is safe, surrounding communities have experienced catastrophic losses. She emphasized that the scale of destruction will require years of recovery work. "Seeing the devastation, I know this is going to take decades to recover. We as a country don't have the resources," Navarro said. Marino highlighted the organization's commitment to directing aid efficiently. "The only thing that I can do is do our best to come together and help them and find different resources so we can get it directly to the people and bring the help that they need," she said. The organizers are partnering with Global Empowerment Mission to transport collected supplies to Venezuela, and they guarantee that 100 percent of donations will go through verified humanitarian relief channels.

The relief drive is seeking a comprehensive range of supplies to address urgent needs. Items being collected include powder Gatorade, non-perishable food items, baby formula and baby food, diapers in all sizes, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids. According to Marino, hundreds of thousands of people currently need assistance. Navarro identified the most critical shortages, stating "the worst is the food and the place to sleep, to take a bath. They don't have that right now."

The organizers emphasize that the relief drive welcomes support from the entire community. "We are asking not just the Hispanic community, we are asking everyone. They really need us," the founders said. Those wishing to contribute or coordinate donations can contact Lourana Navarro at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747.

cards.headline: 2 people killed in head-on crash on Allapattah Road in Indiantown
cards.teaser: Two people died Saturday morning in a head-on collision along the Allapattah S-Curve near Martin Highway in Indiantown.
cards.body: Two people were killed in a head-on crash along Allapattah Road, also known as the Allapattah S-Curve, near Martin Highway in Indiantown on Saturday morning. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the crash occurred around 6:30 a.m. at 8113 SW Allapattah Road. The road was blocked for about 6 hours while the Florida Highway Patrol processed the scene and has since reopened.

cards.headline: Off-duty Martin County Fire Rescue lieutenant recovers body of missing diver found dead near Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet Friday, recovered by an off-duty Martin Co.
cards.body:
A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet Friday. The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding the missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed 4 vessels to assist in the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit, which had independently monitored the Mayday call, was already en route to assist.

Martin County Fire Rescue Lt. Daniel DeGrazia was called in at 1:30 p.m. Friday to assist with recovery efforts. DeGrazia was off-duty at the time and assisted by his own will. Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park. At approximately 4:15 p.m., DeGrazia recovered the body of the missing diver at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver had drowned and was pronounced deceased. The deceased was transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is the lead agency on the investigation. The victim's name is expected to be released Monday.

hero.headline: Vero Beach MusicWorks launches 14th concert season to boost cultural tourism
hero.body:
MusicWorks in Vero Beach is launching its fourteenth concert season, positioning Florida alongside California, Texas, New York, Tennessee, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, Arizona, Michigan and Massachusetts in an effort to expand cultural tourism and inspire multi-state travel. The concert series aims to draw visitors from across the country to the Treasure Coast for live performances.

The announcement marks more than a decade of programming by the Vero Beach organization, which has established itself as a regional cultural destination. The season launch aligns Florida with major cultural hubs across the nation, suggesting a coordinated effort to attract music enthusiasts to the state.

Cultural tourism has become an increasingly important economic driver for Florida communities, with concerts and arts programming bringing overnight visitors who spend money on hotels, restaurants and local businesses. Vero Beach, located in Indian River County, has worked to diversify its tourism beyond beaches and golf.

The fourteenth season programming details and performance dates were not disclosed in the announcement. MusicWorks has built a reputation for bringing professional-caliber performances to the Treasure Coast, serving residents and visitors in Indian River County and surrounding areas.

cards.headline: George Snow Scholarship Fund awards record $7.5 million to 470 Palm Beach and Broward students
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton-based George Snow Scholarship Fund reached a milestone in 2026, distributing more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to students across two South Florida counties.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund, headquartered in Boca Raton, awarded a record $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, President Tim Snow told WPTV. Founded over 40 years ago, the nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. The program offers four-year commitments to ensure stability throughout college and is designed to bridge the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford.

GSSF's services extend beyond financial assistance, providing mentorship, professional development, and resources like the College Compass podcast, according to Vice President of Development Jay Brandt. One 2026 recipient, Zya Chow, a Wellington Community High School graduate, earned both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship and plans to attend Georgetown University. The fund also operates the Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, led by Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine, which offers professional, formal, and casual wear for interviews, internships, and campus life. The boutique accepts donations of new or gently used clothing, footwear, and accessories.

cards.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League urges Treasure Coast pet owners to prepare for hurricane season
cards.teaser: With hurricane season underway, Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is calling on South Florida residents to create disaster plans for their pets before the next storm arrives.
cards.body:
Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League, told WPTV the safest place for pets during a hurricane is right alongside their owners. The shelter is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before the next storm hits with several key recommendations.

Pet owners should ensure their animals wear a collar with current identification and have an updated microchip registered with correct contact information. The shelter recommends introducing pets to a designated safe room ahead of time, such as a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom, and conducting practice runs so the hurricane is not their first time there. A pet emergency kit should include a three-day supply of food and water in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, first-aid supplies, litter and box for cats, leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, waste bags, and multiple forms of visible ID. Pet owners should keep a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels in an accessible place and maintain recent photos of pets, ideally with their owner, to help with identification if separated. Florida's hurricane season runs June through November.

cards.headline: Elliott Museum to host two global 3-D immersion exhibits
cards.teaser: Two international exhibits featuring 3-D immersion technology are coming to the Elliott Museum on the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
The Elliott Museum will host two global exhibits featuring 3-D immersion technology, expanding cultural programming available to Treasure Coast residents. The museum, located in Stuart, is bringing the international exhibitions to Martin County.

The 3-D immersion format represents a growing trend in museum programming, offering visitors interactive experiences that differ from traditional gallery displays. The Elliott Museum has established itself as a regional cultural destination in Martin County, drawing visitors from across the Treasure Coast and beyond with rotating exhibitions alongside its permanent collections.

cards.headline: Attorney General Ashley Moody joins Doral volunteers packing earthquake aid for Venezuela
cards.teaser: U.S. Attorney General Ashley Moody assisted in relief efforts from South Florida this weekend as Venezuelans search for missing victims in the aftermath of devastating earthquakes.
cards.body:
Attorney General Ashley Moody assisted in relief efforts for Venezuela on Saturday while in Doral at a staging area for the Global Empowerment Mission. Moody and her husband, Justin Duralia, helped pack containers of food and other boxes of relief goods bound for areas affected by earthquakes that struck the South American country this past week. "Florida stands with the Venezuelan people. Justin and I were inspired by the dedicated and passionate volunteers that gathered to donate and assemble aid for the Venezuelan people reeling from the devastating earthquakes," Moody said in a news release.

The Global Empowerment Mission, founded in Doral, specializes in rapid relief for disaster victims and provides long-term recovery assistance for natural disasters and other humanitarian crises including conflicts. The situation in Venezuela remains dire as tens of thousands of people remain missing following back-to-back earthquakes that struck Wednesday. More than 1,400 people have been confirmed dead. On Friday night, Venezuelan authorities announced they would block off access to La Guaira, the epicenter of destruction, requiring official permits for entry as chaos and traffic affected search efforts. Citizens digging through rubble reported seeing few state rescue teams in the hardest hit areas despite the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes.

cards.headline: DeSantis praises World Cup visitors while reflecting on divisive political rhetoric
cards.teaser: Ron DeSantis praised the World Cup for giving visiting fans from other countries a chance to see America directly, saying visitors have gotten to see firsthand the generosity of the American people and that this is a good country.
cards.body:
Ron DeSantis praised the World Cup for giving visiting fans from other countries a chance to see America firsthand. "We do have a really great country. I know there's a lot of problems. I know we see a lot of things that we wish we could change immediately," DeSantis said. "But I wouldn't want to be anywhere else." The visitors have gotten to see both the generosity of the American people and that this is a good country, he added. The World Cup created a setting in which people from Scotland, Iran, Brazil, Morocco, and Australia arrived with impressions shaped by their own politics and media, then discovered something different.

However, DeSantis's own political brand, which got him elected twice and made him one of the most influential governors in the country, is built substantially on the premise that a vast, organized internal enemy is destroying America. Teachers who discussed gender identity were characterized as "groomers," and corporate executives supporting diversity programs were called carriers of the "woke mind virus." President Trump has made the same argument in far more extreme terms, declaring a pledge to "root out the communists, Marxists, fascists and the radical left thugs that live like vermin within the confines of our country" at a November 2023 campaign rally in New Hampshire. A month later, he described immigrants arriving in the United States as "poisoning the blood of our country," a phrase with historic parallels.

cards.headline: Iran attacks Bahrain and Kuwait, threatens to halt talks over U.S. strikes
cards.teaser: Iran launched drone and missile attacks Sunday targeting Bahrain and Kuwait in response to new U.S. airstrikes against the Islamic Republic and threatened a complete halt in negotiations to end the war if Washington continues its attacks.
cards.body:
Iran launched drone and missile attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait on Sunday in response to U.S. airstrikes, while threatening a "complete halt" to negotiations aimed at ending the war. The Iranian paramilitary Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for the attacks. Kuwait's military said air defenses intercepted Iranian drones and missiles, with two ballistic missiles intercepted, while reporting no injuries or damage. Bahrain's Interior Ministry said Iranian strikes damaged a residential building near the international airport with no deaths, releasing photos showing an eight-story building with its top floor destroyed and windows blown out. The U.S. military's Central Command said it struck Iranian military surveillance infrastructure, communication systems, air defense sites, drone storage facilities and minelayer capabilities following an attack on the Panamanian-flagged tanker Kiku, which carried crude oil for Qatar's state energy company.

Disputes over the Strait of Hormuz governance have sparked the crossfire and imperiled ceasefire talks. A multinational maritime body overseen by the U.S. Navy said Saturday it would expand a route near Oman for inbound and outbound traffic. Iran insists it alone must govern the strait, the narrow mouth of the Persian Gulf that once carried a fifth of the world's oil and natural gas. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said any attempt to establish separate arrangements would increase tension and delay reopening the strait. The United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding this month giving them 60 days to finalize terms including shipping arrangements, removal of a U.S. blockade on Iranian ports and Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile.

cards.headline: Largo Mayor reads Pride Month proclamation after planned cancellation draws crowd
cards.teaser: Largo Mayor Woody Brown opened the June 2 Commission meeting by reading a Pride Month proclamation, a gesture the city had planned to drop from the agenda entirely before word got out and dozens of residents showed up to object.
cards.body:
Largo Mayor Woody Brown read a Pride Month proclamation at the June 2 Commission meeting after the city initially planned to remove it from the agenda. Dozens of residents showed up to object to the cancellation. Many attendees arrived directly from the ribbon-cutting for Horizon West Bay, the $85 million mixed-use development anchored by the city's new City Hall, and used their public comment time to express their concerns about the proclamation's removal.

The same Commission recently passed an ordinance creating a new open-container entertainment district called Sip and Stroll in the blocks surrounding City Hall. The program allows patrons to walk freely through designated downtown zones with drinks purchased from approved local businesses. Abner Morales, who owns Wepaa Puerto Rican Restaurant nearby, is already designing custom branded cups for the district. Brown explained in a June 1 online chat that new legislation barring local governments from spending on diversity, equity and inclusion-related events doesn't take effect until January. However, with the budget still unsigned, Brown said the Governor could cut off funding streams Largo depends on, including dollars for stormwater infrastructure.

cards.headline: Ship traffic increases on Strait of Hormuz despite elevated threat from Iran
cards.teaser: Ship traffic on the Strait of Hormuz increased over the past 72 hours, off both Iran and Oman, as U.S.-assisted commercial transits continued uninterrupted despite the elevated threat environment.
cards.body:
A multinational maritime body overseen by the U.S. Navy said Sunday that 89 transits had been made through the Strait of Hormuz over the past 72 hours, still below the historical average of 138 vessels a day. Despite the elevated threat environment, U.S.-assisted commercial transits continued uninterrupted. The global community has long considered the strait an international passageway, despite its location in Iran and Oman's territorial waters. In recent days, Iran has twice attacked vessels going through a route on the Omani side in an evacuation effort backed by a United Nations agency.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reiterated Iran's claim that it alone must govern the strait. "Any attempt to establish new or separate arrangements from those currently being carried out by the Islamic Republic of Iran will only lead to further complications, delay the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and increase the level of tension," Araghchi said. The United States and Iran have been debating the terms of an interim deal, including shipping arrangements on the strait, removal of a U.S. blockade on Iranian ports, sanctions on Iran and the future of Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Under the memorandum of understanding signed this month, they have 60 days to iron out details. The interim deal is meant to end fighting on all fronts before certain key issues can be discussed. Continued fighting in Lebanon, where an Israeli soldier was killed by Hezbollah fire early Sunday, also threatens the agreement.

cards.headline: Jupiter firefighters deploy to Venezuela for earthquake rescue operations
cards.teaser: Jupiter Fire Rescue sent two firefighters to Venezuela as part of an 80-member FEMA search and rescue team responding to earthquake damage.
cards.body:
First responders from Jupiter, Delray Beach, and Palm Beach County fire departments have deployed to Venezuela as part of a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force to assist with earthquake relief efforts. Jupiter Fire Rescue deployed two firefighters as part of a crew of 80 that was sent with less than 24 hours notice and is expected to remain in Venezuela for at least two weeks.

The mission focuses on search and rescue operations in collapsed structures, ranging from large buildings to smaller homes. The team brought heavy-duty equipment for breaking, cutting, breaching, and stabilization, as well as technical rope rescue tools. Stephen Shaw, deputy fire chief of operations for Jupiter Fire Rescue, said the deployment reflects the department's commitment to helping those in need. Shaw noted that the experience will also strengthen the department when the crew returns home, as the learning and skills practiced will benefit Jupiter Fire Rescue internally as the department continues to grow.

cards.headline: Off-duty Martin County firefighter recovers body of diver who drowned near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: The St.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is investigating after a missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding the missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed 4 vessels to assist in the search. FWC personnel also contacted the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit, which had independently monitored the Mayday call and was already en route to assist.

Martin County Fire Rescue Lt. Daniel DeGrazia was called in at 1:30 p.m. Friday to assist with recovery efforts. DeGrazia was off-duty at the time and assisted by his own will. Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park. At approximately 4:15 p.m., DeGrazia recovered the body of the missing diver, who had drowned, at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver was pronounced deceased and transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is the lead agency on the investigation. The victim's name was not available Saturday afternoon, with an update expected Monday.
